Hi Elena — thanks for the diagram and the clear list. I've attached our onboarding checklist (redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf) and pasted the concise preflight we use below so your engineers can action items quickly. I also dropped a draft mutual action plan link (see related links) — we can convert to a tracked doc.

Redwood preflight (what we need from Aurora) — concise checklist:
1) Network reachability
   - Provide egress IP range(s) for your firewall allowlist (we'll provide our egress set for callbacks)
   - Confirm VPC peering / routing map or shared VPC approach (include route table IDs)
   - NAT / SNAT behavior and MTU if nonstandard
2) Access & credentials
   - Create a Redwood service account with owner/editor + logging role OR supply a short-lived access key as discussed
   - KMS: either share a key ARN with cross-account grant, or confirm Redwood-managed key usage (we need key rotation policy and contact)
3) Security & observability
   - Provide SOC2 or equivalent cert copies if available for any third-party infrastructure in the chain
   - Enable flow logs for the deployment subnet for at least 72 hours pre-cutover
4) Environment & test data
   - Provide a test user set and sample payloads (PII should be scrubbed)
   - Define SLO targets for canary (p50/p95 latency, qps) — we recommend p95 < 300ms for gen requests on the canary model profile
5) Scheduling
   - Proposed canary week: Oct 6 — Redwood ops can allocate a 4-hour smoke window and a rolling 48-hour observation window after cutover. Please confirm timezone and blackout windows.

Action owners (example):
- Aurora: Elena, Platform team — egress list, IAM, KMS
- Redwood: Markus (overall), Ben (network), Kimberly (security evidence)

Please reply in-thread with any items you can't provide and we'll propose alternatives (e.g., temporary SSH jumpbox for KMS test, stubbed traffic for smoke).

Attachments: redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Markus Klein

Elena — quick network clarifications from our side (keeping short):

- We'll need the full egress CIDR list in CIDR format (comma-separated) so we can validate NAT mapping and update the firewall rules on our end. Example format: 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.128/25
- If you're using asymmetric routing or any third-party transit, call that out — it changes how we schedule peering tests
- MTU: if any segment is <1500, note that now; we sometimes see reassembly issues with large token payloads

Proposed smoke test checklist (we'll run during the 4-hour window):
- TLS handshake and end-to-end request (sanity)
- 10 concurrent synthetic requests at canary model profile for 10 mins (observe p50/p95)
- KV cache warm-up test (time to steady-state)
- Telemetry sanity: trace, span, token-level cost tag present

I've attached a CSV with our suggested egress ranges that we will use for callbacks if you want to map locally: egress_ip_ranges.csv

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
